newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks show mild downward correction.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks show mild downward correction.

text.p: Argentine stocks pulled back gently Tuesday after recent strong gains and traders welcomed the fall as a healthy correction.

"The market topped out when it pierced 800 points and started a technical correction," said Miguel Daneri of Boston Securities. "It's a very mild fall which isn't a threat -- the underlying trend remains firm thanks to strong international cash flows and local pension fund investments."
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV shed 0.4 percent to 788.73, pulling off a floor of 786.81. It had peaked at 801.35 early in the session.
"I expect some more profit taking tomorrow but not a strong fall. Sentiment remains very good," another trader said.
The MerVal halted a three-session rally during which it rose 4.2 percent, and recorded its third loss in 17 sessions.
"We don't like it when the market rises for too long without a break, so you could say this loss rather than going against the trend, is favoring it," Daneri said.
He noted volume remained strong and stock purchases, not sales, accounted for the majority of transactions. "The correction was for dealers and small investors," Daneri said.

Traders also said that, even though the bolsa has come unhinged from Wall Street recently on the back of ground- breaking corporate news, including big bank mergers, the fall in U.S. long bond yields to 6.87 percent from more than 7.0 percent just last Wednesday helped to underpin the bolsa.
"The long bond yield seems to have 7.0 percent as a ceiling again, which should help buffer any deeper correction here," a trader said.
The broad market matched MerVal losses of 0.4 percent, but rises beat declines 41 to 23 and 17 issues closed flat.

Floor volume remained strong at 40.5 million pesos against 40.2 million Monday, but over-the-counter turnover shrank to 113.5 millon from Monday's huge tally of 315.7 million, attributed partially to end-of-month position squaring.

Top MerVal risers were real estate developer Irsa, up 2.7 percent, petrochemical firm Indupa, up 2.4 percent and cement firm Juan Minetti, up 1.6 percent. Bellwether oil giant YPF rose 1.5 percent to a new record close of $30.55. Losers were led by Telefonica, Banco de Galicia and oil firm Astra, off 2.9 percent, 2.3 percent and 2.2 percent, respectively.
